description:
Accademia Carrara in Bergamo grew from the collection of Giacomo Carrara, who founded it in 1796. Later bequests made private collecting central to the museum’s character.

Its paintings trace Italian art from the Gothic period to the nineteenth century. Lombard and Venetian traditions are especially important, including works by Lorenzo Lotto, Giovanni Bellini and Giovan Battista Moroni.

description:

Milan’s Galleria d’Arte Moderna is housed in the Villa Reale on Via Palestro. Its collections explore nineteenth-century art, from Neoclassicism and Romanticism to Divisionism and Symbolism.
